papers.title: Dominoes tiling a common figure
papers.abstract: Call a two-element subset of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ a domino. Given finitely many dominoes $D_1,\ldots,D_k$, we show that there exists a finite non-empty $B\subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ such that $B$ can be partitioned into disjoint translates of $D_i$ for all $i$. The proof uses a new absorption mechanism for perfect matchings in algebraically defined hypergraphs.

papers.title: Abelian envelopes and quantum groups in Knop's interpolation categories
papers.abstract: We show the existence of abelian envelopes for large classes of subcategories of Knop's tensor envelopes. It follows that these abelian envelopes correspond to groups or more generally Hopf algebras (``quantum groups'') in their parent interpolation categories. As a special case, we obtain that the interpolation categories in the sense of Flake--Maassen (2022) of all so-called group-theoretical easy quantum groups have abelian envelopes given by quantum groups in Deligne's interpolation category of the symmetric groups. Similarly, we apply our theory to interpolation categories of wreath products, finite general linear groups, and finite affine groups. Our main technique is an explicit construction of objects corresponding to coordinate algebras using the calculus of relations that Knop's categories are based on.

papers.title: A canonical Euclidean Gallai theorem
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove a canonical Euclidean Gallai theorem: for any finite set of points $S\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, any colouring of $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a scaled (and possibly rotated) copy of $S$ that is either monochromatic or rainbow.

papers.title: Energy and topology of Ricci-flat 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that there is $C>0$ such that any complete Ricci-flat $4$-manifold $(M,g)$ satisfies $$ b_2(M)-C\leqslant\frac1{8π^2}\int_M|R_g|_g^2\,dv_g\leqslant b_2(M)+C, $$ where $R$ is the curvature operator. No assumption is made on volume growth, model at infinity or curvature decay. It follows that uncountably many exotic $\mathbb R^4$ admit no complete Ricci-flat metric, and that complete noncompact hyperkähler metrics with finite $b_2$ have ends classified by Sun-Zhang. This also provides information about the thin part of immortal four-dimensional Ricci flows in Bamler's decomposition. The proof refines the chopping method of Cheeger-Gromov and Cheeger-Tian by bounding the topology of boundaries of regions exhausting the manifold.

papers.title: Winning and losing NoGo is PSPACE-complete
papers.abstract: We resolve an open problem of Burke and Hearn and show that the combinatorial game NoGo is PSPACE-complete on grids. This is the usual geometry the game is played on, including at the tournament at a 2011 Banff workshop. In addition to this result, we show that it is also PSPACE-complete under misère play on grids. We prove both of these results using reductions from Bounded Two-Player Constraint Logic. Finally, we show that it is PSPACE-complete under normal play on connected bipartite subcubic graphs.

papers.title: Non-formality of prefactorization algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a Poisson bracket on the cohomology of locally constant prefactorization algebras on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that provides an obstruction to formality in every dimension $m\geqslant 2$. Our construction combines colored obstruction sequences to formality with linking spheres and generalizes the two-dimensional bracket of Bruinsma, Schenkel, and Vicedo. We use it to extend their non-formality theorem for Lie algebra factorization envelopes to all higher dimensions. We also establish new non-formality results for factorization envelopes of Lie algebras, their compactifications and generalizations to $L_\infty$-algebras, free BF-type theories, higher abelian Chern-Simons theories and their compactifications.

papers.title: Efficient reconfiguration, polynomial decompositions and approximate counting
papers.abstract: We consider reconfigurations of integer assignments to planar lattice regions that preserve specified line totals, which are motivated by questions of combinatorial construction, algorithmic sampling and approximate counting. An elementary prototype is provided by contingency tables, i.e. two-dimensional grids of non-negative integers with prescribed row and column sums, which can be reconfigured by basic switches of the form $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. More difficult combinatorial instances include reconfiguration of Latin squares or queens configurations. Our main technical ingredient is the following polynomial decomposition lemma. Fix a positive integer $k$. Let $F(x)\in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be a polynomial of degree at most $n$ such that $(1-x)^k\mid F(x)$ and the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients of $F$ is $m$. We prove that $F$ can be written as a sum of $O(m+n)$ basic polynomials of degree at most $n$ of the form $\pm x^a(1-x^{a_1})\cdots (1-x^{a_k})$ where $a,a_1,\ldots,a_k$ are non-negative integers. The proof uses the existence of a miraculous high-dimensional coupling of signed distributions on cross polytopes that has independent interest. We will apply this lemma to questions of combinatorial construction in other papers; in this paper we illustrate its application to approximate counting.

papers.title: Brauer classes of representations of division algebras and their Langlands parameters
papers.abstract: For every depth-zero supercuspidal representation $π$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ with algebraic-valued central character, we prove that the Brauer obstructions to realizing its Jacquet-Langlands transfer and its normalized Langlands parameter $\varphi_π\otimes|\cdot|^{-(n-1)/2}$ over their common field of rationality $E=\mathbb{Q}(π)$ sum to $(n-1)[B_{p,\infty}\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} E]$. Here $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ is finite, the transfer is to the units of the central division algebra over $K$ of invariant $1/n$, and $B_{p,\infty}$ is the quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$ ramified exactly at $p$ and $\infty$. We conjecture this identity without the depth restriction. For arbitrarily large $n=p-1$, we construct simple supercuspidal representations satisfying the same sum formula. Their transfers have finite-order central character and Schur index $n$, whereas their normalized parameters have index $n/2$. Since these transfers are not self-dual, the unequal indices contradict the isomorphism of Schur algebras conjectured by Prasad and Ramakrishnan.

papers.title: Forms and polynomial covers in many variables
papers.abstract: Let $F \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a homogeneous form of degree $d \ge 2$, and let $σ$ be the affine dimension of the singular locus of $F = 0$. We prove that the hypersurface $F = 0$ satisfies the smooth Hasse principle whenever \[ n - σ\ge 2^{d + 1} - 3. \] This is the first improvement in the order of magnitude of Birch's classical result. We also apply the method to the counting problem for polynomial covers $F(x_1,\ldots,x_n) = g(y)$, and give a condition on $n - σ$ under which Serre's conjectural upper bound holds and another condition under which the expected asymptotic formula holds.

papers.title: Max-degree filtration, Koszul complexes, and Multicolor Permutation Wordle
papers.abstract: We explore the Koszul resolutions of a family of ideals, each generated by multivariate polynomials that split completely into linear factors. The motivating examples come from the game Permutation Wordle of Kutin and Smithline, as analyzed by Kutin, Smithline, and Vatter, and an open question, Conjecture 4.5 in Kutin and Smithline's work on Multicolor Permutation Wordle. For each ideal in this family, with our chosen generators, the Koszul differentials are strict for the max-degree filtration and, more generally, at every multidegree whose coordinates form a set of consecutive integers. The resulting dimension count resolves Kutin and Smithline's conjecture. The proof is an induction in which each inductive step is an iteration. The core argument is human generated. The present proof, developed with AI assistance, separates the iteration of multidegree reductions from the mapping cone induction. This method avoids the need to chase compatibility of lifts up to the top grade of the complex.

papers.title: Large blow-ups of uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: Let \(k\ge2\), let \(H\) be a fixed \(k\)-uniform hypergraph on \(h\) vertices with at least one edge, and let \(a>0\). We prove that every sufficiently large \(n\)-vertex \(k\)-uniform hypergraph with at least \(a n^h\) copies of \(H\) contains a blow-up of \(H\) with at least \(b(\log n)^{1/(k-1)}\) vertices in each part, where \(b=b(H,a)>0\). The exponent of $\log n$ is best possible. This answers a question of Rödl and Schacht and proves a conjecture of Bollobás, Erdős and Simonovits from 1976. For fixed \(q\ge2\) and \(0<α<1/2\), it follows that every \(q\)-coloring of the \(k\)-subsets of \([n]\) contains a set of order \((\log n)^{1/(k-1)}\) on which one color has density at least \(1-α\). For triples this recovers the sharp bound of Conlon, Fox and Sudakov. For \(k\ge4\), this improves their general exponent to the optimal value \(1/(k-1)\) and answers a 1990 question of Erdős for which he offered a \$500 prize.

papers.title: An internal approach to symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories
papers.abstract: We propose a definition of symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories as special left double $(\infty,n)$-fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The definition makes sense in a general model of $(\infty,n)$-categories, under a mild condition on its discrete objects, and when the model is left proper and combinatorial we construct model structures whose fibrant objects are exactly these fibrations. For $n=1$ we show that the definition recovers Lurie's symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories: the homotopy theory of special left double $(\infty,1)$-fibrations is equivalent to that of special coCartesian fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The equivalence is realized by an explicit Quillen equivalence, and two constructions, the staircase and coCartesian strings, translate between the two descriptions.

papers.title: The tower transition in majority bootstrap percolation
papers.abstract: How large must a high-dimensional torus be for majority bootstrap percolation to fill it at a given density below one half? For a torus of side length $n\ge3$, let $H(n)$ be the smallest $h$ such that a tower of $h$ twos has value at least $n$. If $H(n)/d\toρ\in[0,1]$, the critical density on the $d$-dimensional torus tends to $(1-ρ)/(2-ρ)$. In particular, the smallest side length $n$ for which the critical density is at most $1/4$ satisfies $H(n)\sim 2d/3$. The same curve holds for ordinary boxes of side at least $d$. For boxes with $n/d\to a>0$ we obtain the limiting density $\max\{1/2,1-2^{-1/a}\}$. We determine the first correction to the tower curve away from $ρ=1$.

papers.title: One-Relator Products of Left-Orderable Groups
papers.abstract: We prove that, for left-orderable groups $A,B$ and a word $w\in A*B$ which is not conjugate into $A$ or $B$ and is not a proper power, the one-relator product $A*B/\left\langle\!\left\langle w \right\rangle\!\right\rangle$ is torsion-free, answering a question posed by Chen and Lodha. We do this by proving a relative asphericity result for the one-relator product. We also generalise the B. B. Newman Spelling Theorem to one-relator products and deduce that a one-relator product $A*B/\left\langle\!\left\langle w^k \right\rangle\!\right\rangle$ of left-orderable groups with torsion is hyperbolic relative to $\{A,B\}$.

papers.title: Quaternionic geometry of symplectic and contact pairs
papers.abstract: We introduce quaternionic analogues of symplectic pairs, contact--symplectic pairs and contact pairs. A hyper symplectic pair consists of three symplectic pairs whose sums form a positive quaternionic triple, while the contact analogues are defined through single or double symplectization. We prove that radial invariance of the induced complex structures is equivalent to the coincidence of the characteristic distributions, yielding a local product decomposition. Under a natural normalization, hyper contact--symplectic pairs are locally products of a $3$-Sasakian and a hyper-Kähler manifold and induce canonical $3$-quasi-Sasakian structures, whereas hyper contact pairs are locally products of two $3$-Sasakian manifolds. We construct compact examples for which these local decompositions are not global. Finally, compact normalized hyper contact pairs have finite fundamental group and are finite quotients of products of compact $3$-Sasakian manifolds, in contrast with normalized hyper contact--symplectic pairs, which may have infinite fundamental group.

papers.title: DEC Fill-ins, the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, and positive mass theorems with untrapped boundary
papers.abstract: Given a closed $(n-1)$-dimensional manifold equipped with prescribed spacetime Bartnik data, we ask when this can be realised as the boundary of a compact $n$-dimensional initial data set satisfying the dominant energy condition (DEC). This is a natural generalisation of the problem of non-negative scalar curvature fill-ins, where the boundary metric and mean curvature are prescribed. We give conditions on the Bartnik data that suffice to prove the existence of such DEC fill-ins with inner MOTS boundary, and give some applications of these fill-ins. Our first application of these is a lower bound on the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, which we slightly reformulate here to be a genuine spacetime definition. Our other applications include proving a positive mass theorem for spin initial data with boundary that need not be trapped, and a spacetime Penrose-like inequality that gives a positive lower bound on the mass of an initial data set with boundary in terms of its boundary Bartnik data assuming the spacetime Penrose inequality holds.

papers.title: Properties of the Sawin--Wood Model for Unramified Galois Groups of Global Fields
papers.abstract: We prove almost-sure finite generation and finite presentation in the pro-$|Γ|'$ $Γ$-category for the Sawin--Wood measure $ν_{Γ,n,U}$, where $Γ$ is a non-trivial finite group, $n$ is coprime to $|Γ|$, and $U$ is a nonempty multiset of conjugacy classes of $Γ$. The $Γ$-generator rank of the random group $X$ has the sharp tail $\mathbf{P}(d_Γ(X) \geq r) = Ce^{-κr^2-ζr}(1+O(e^{-\varepsilon r}))$, where $C>0$, $κ>0$, and $ζ\in\mathbb{R}$ are explicit constants depending on $n$, $Γ$ and $U$, and $\varepsilon>0$. Almost surely, $X$ admits a presentation with the minimum number of $Γ$-generators, using at most $|U|$ more defining $Γ$-relations than generators. We also prove that every open subgroup of $X$ has finite abelianization almost surely under the assumption that for every complex representation of $Γ$ there is an element in $U$ that fixes a nonzero vector. Finally, we prove that $H_2(X,\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})=0$ almost surely when $n=1$, $Γ$ is cyclic, and $U$ contains only the conjugacy class of a generator of $Γ$ (with multiplicity one).

papers.title: Rank 1 composition factors in the polydisk
papers.abstract: For an isometry-invariant reproducing kernel $k$ on the unit polydisk $\mathbb{D}^d$, we consider its composition factors, analytic selfmaps $φ:\mathbb{D}^d\to\mathbb{D}^d$ such that $k^φ=k/(k\circφ)$ is a reproducing kernel. Denoting its corresponding Hilbert space by $\mathcal{H}(k^φ)$, we define the rank of $φ$ with respect to $k$ as the dimension of $\mathcal{H}(k^φ)$. Using these notions, we reframe recent work considering co-isometric weighted composition operators in the unit disk by Mas, Martín, and Vukotić, and in the unit ball by Hartz and Tornes. That is, we illustrate a bijective correspondence between the above operators and rank $1$ composition operators, and extend their results to the setting of the polydisk. Namely, supposing that $φ$ is a rank $1$ composition factor of $k$ and assuming that $k$ is either bounded or unbounded everywhere on $\partial\mathbb{D}^d$, we prove that $φ$ must be an automorphism. Moreover, if it is not a composition of a rotation and permutation, then $k$ must be a positive power of the Szegő kernel. We also briefly consider finite rank composition factors.

papers.title: $S$-preclones and the Galois connection ${}^S\mathrm{Pol}$-${}^S\mathrm{Inv}$, Part II: Boolean $\pm$-preclones
papers.abstract: We continue the investigation of $S$-preclones initiated in Part I, specializing to the case of Boolean $\pm$-preclones where $S = \{+,-\}$ is the two-element group and the base set is $A = \{0,1\}$. The main results include the complete classification of maximal and minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones in the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ of all Boolean $\pm$-preclones. We prove that there are exactly nine maximal Boolean $\pm$-preclones. Hence we obtain a completeness theorem for $\pm$-preclones: a set of $\pm$-operations generates all $\pm$-operations if and only if it contains an operation that fails to preserve each of the nine defining $\pm$-relations of the maximal $\pm$-preclones. Next we classify the twenty minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones (atoms of the lattice), each described via a generating $\pm$-operation. We also investigate self-dual $\pm$-preclones, characterizing the eight maximal and nine minimal self-dual $\pm$-preclones and proving a corresponding completeness theorem. Additionally, we include the result, due to Vojtěch David, that the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ is uncountable, in contrast with the countability of the classical Post lattice of Boolean clones. This is established by embedding an uncountable poset of clonoids into ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$. Finally, we study preimage classes of classical Boolean clones within ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$, providing complete descriptions for the unary case and for several non-unary minimal clones. We also prove a Baker--Pixley type theorem for $\pm$-preclones containing the majority operation, showing that such $\pm$-preclones are determined by their binary $\pm$-relations.

papers.title: An $A_1$ characterization of the boundedness of the maximal function on weighted variable Lebesgue spaces
papers.abstract: We characterize the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M$ on weighted variable Lebesgue spaces for exponents satisfying $1<p_-\le p_+<\infty$. We show that $M$ is bounded on $L^{p(\cdot)}_w$ if and only if the pair $(p(\cdot),w)$ satisfies a variable Muckenhoupt condition and there exists $h\in L^1$ such that $w^{-1}h^{1/p(\cdot)}$ and $wh^{1/p'(\cdot)}$ belong to $A_1$. This characterization is new even in the unweighted setting. To prove sufficiency, we use sparse domination together with a local modular averaging estimate whose error terms are summable over sparse families to $\|h\|_{L^1}$. Conversely, assuming $M$ is bounded, we construct $h$ using a simultaneous Rubio de Francia algorithm. To motivate this new characterization, we show that the strong Muckenhoupt condition, which characterizes the boundedness of $M$ in the unweighted case by a theorem of Diening, is not sufficient in the weighted setting. As applications, we give short proofs and extensions of known sufficient conditions.

papers.title: Undershoot of h-fold sumsets: Apéry spectra, similar ordering and the three-distance theorem
papers.abstract: For a finite set $A_0\subset\mathbb{N}$ with $0\in A_0$, $\max A_0=d$ and $\gcd(A_0)=1$, and a target $T$, the undershoot at level $h$ is the distance from $T$ down to the largest element of the $h$-fold sumset $hA_0$ not above $T$. Its total over $T\in[0,hd]$ is bounded in $h$: for large $h$ it equals the sum of the masses of two numerical semigroups attached to $A_0$, where the mass adds $L(L+1)/2$ over the maximal runs of $L$ gaps. We describe how the total reaches this limit: it can rise to it, fall to it, or climb past it and return. When the monomial curve of $A_0$ is arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, two Apéry sets give every undershoot exactly, and partial sums of a fixed spectrum bound the total from below, with equality at every level exactly when two threshold sequences are similarly ordered; the total then rises concavely to its limit, reached exactly at the sumsets regularity. We characterize the similarly ordered four-element sets. For $\{0,a,b,2b\}$ with $0<a<b$ coprime, the three-distance theorem gives the total in explicit quadratic pieces. A non-Cohen-Macaulay set exceeds its limit at every failing level $h$ with $hd$ at least the sum of the two conductors; every such four-element set does so, and a five-element example never does. For arbitrary sets, finite corner data give the exact undershoot over any window.

papers.title: Prismatic construction of crystalline deformation rings up to p-power torsion
papers.abstract: We study the deformation of Galois representations which are etale realizations of finitely generated prismatic F-crystals and show the deformation functor is pro-represented by a complete Noetherian local ring whose Z_p-flat quotient coincides with Kisin's crystalline deformation ring. As a consequence, we obtain a universal prismatic F-crystal with coefficients in Kisin's crystalline deformation ring.

papers.title: Bloch Discriminants of Discrete Periodic Operators
papers.abstract: The Bloch variety of an operator on a periodic graph encodes the relation between its spectrum and the group action on the graph, with critical points corresponding to edges of the spectrum. We adapt methods from computational algebraic geometry to describe how the qualitative behavior of critical points of Bloch varieties depends upon parameters for three Z^2-periodic graphs. The set of parameters where the qualitative behavior changes is the Bloch discriminant. As the critical points are real-algebraic with respect to a non-standard real structure on the complex torus, this is also a first step towards developing computational tools for varieties with a non-standard real structure.

papers.title: Perfect powers with small exponents from products of terms in progression
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a large integer, and let $\ell$ be an integer with $2 \leq \ell \leq (\log \log k)^{1/5}$. We determine all solutions to the Diophantine equation \begin{align*} n(n+d)\cdots (n+(k-1)d)=y^\ell \end{align*} in nonzero integers $n,d,y$ with $d\geq 1$ and $\text{gcd}(n,d)=1$. We also prove results for generalizations where the product $n(n+d)\cdots (n+(k-1)d)$ is ``almost'' a perfect power, rather than exactly a perfect power, and where some of the terms $n+id$ are dropped from the product.

papers.title: Bounded Nörlund operators on Hardy spaces
papers.abstract: We characterize the nonnegative Nörlund matrices that induce bounded operators on Hardy spaces. For $a_n\ge0$ and $a_0>0$, boundedness on one $H^p$, $1<p<\infty$, is equivalent to boundedness on every such space and to a single quadratic testing condition involving the ratios of the partial sums $A_n=\sum_{k=0}^na_k$. The testing constant is comparable to the squared $H^2$ operator norm, with absolute constants. No doubling or monotonicity assumption on the weights is required. The proof combines an exact vector-valued Hankel representation with square-function estimates and a geometric argument showing that the doubling-time endpoints have finite lacunary order. Equivalently, boundedness is characterized by a truncated quadratic block condition on the coefficients of $G_a(z)=\sum_n(a_n/A_n)z^n$. Within the bounded family, $G_a$ belongs to the Bloch space if and only if it belongs to $BMOA$, and this occurs exactly when $(A_n)$ is doubling.

papers.title: The local Weil explicit formula and related structures
papers.abstract: We study the reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces constructed from the local Weil quadratic form associated with the Riemann zeta function. Wherever this form is positive definite, we prove a local explicit formula expressing the Weil distribution in terms of the discrete spectra of self-adjoint extensions of the differentiation operator. We characterize the Riemann hypothesis by the uniform boundedness of the diagonal values of the reproducing kernels. We then study the chain of de Branges spaces and recover the Hamiltonian of the corresponding canonical system explicitly from these kernels under local positivity, without assuming the Riemann hypothesis. Finally, assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we study the asymptotic behavior of solutions of this system.

papers.title: Triangle-free planar graphs need not be POSH
papers.abstract: We show that a triangle-free planar graph need not be partial one-sided Hamiltonian. This disproves a conjecture of Felsner, Schrezenmaier, Schröder and Steiner.

papers.title: On Presburger Arithmetic Expanded with Prime Numbers
papers.abstract: We prove unconditionally that the first-order theory of Presburger arithmetic expanded by a predicate for the primes is undecidable. Bateman, Jockusch and Woods proved this in 1993 assuming Dickson's conjecture. We use the counter-machine framework of Karimov, Nieuwveld and Ouaknine and their idea of using `arbitrary permutations', and the number-theoretic input comes from Hildebrand and Maier's 1988 proof that the limit points of $k$ consecutive normalised prime gaps have positive measure. We use a discrete version, which they obtain before limits are taken. The key lemma is that although Hildebrand and Maier's result does not seem to give arbitrary permutations of consecutive prime gaps, it gives arbitrary permutations for the differences $p_i - q_i$ for two finite blocks of consecutive primes $p_0 < \cdots < p_k$ and $q_0 < \cdots < q_k$. Moreover, with the same key lemma, we show that Presburger arithmetic expanded with the function that maps $n$ to the $n$th prime defines multiplication.

papers.title: Traversing hyperplane arrangements with an affine objective
papers.abstract: We give geometric constructions of directed acyclic graphs on the chambers of a locally finite affine hyperplane arrangement. Fix a nonconstant affine objective. At each chamber where it is bounded above, a choice of flag based at the optimal face determines $2^r-1$ outgoing edges, where $r$ is the codimension of that face. The optimal value of the objective weakly increases on each step, but not always strictly. Nevertheless, we show that every infinite directed walk in these graphs eventually reaches a chamber where the optimal value exceeds its starting value. Additionally, we show that if an affine objective is bounded above on a closed face of a locally finite affine hyperplane arrangement, then the supremum is attained, and the optimizer set is again a closed face, generalizing the classical result for polyhedra.

papers.title: Boomerang identities and binomial transform
papers.abstract: In Pascal's triangle, the boomerang identities, which were recently introduced, combine and extend the well-known hockey-stick identities of the binomial coefficients by allowing additional terms. We show that the binomial transform of sequences in a ring play a central role in this context. Subsequently, we show several applications to Bell and Bernoulli numbers and polynomials, Appell polynomials, as well as, to harmonic, Fibonacci, Lucas, and Stirling numbers.

papers.title: Curvature varifolds with given oriented boundary
papers.abstract: Let $γ\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a closed, embedded, connected, oriented $C^1$ submanifold in $\mathbb R^n$ of dimension $m-1$ where $2\leq m<n$. We prove that the area of any immersed $m$-dimensional submanifold with oriented boundary $γ$ is bounded in terms of its curvature energy, unless $γ$ lies in an $m$-plane. The problems leads to a weak formulation involving oriented curvature varifolds with given oriented boundary, and we solve a boundary-value minimization problem with obstacle in this class.

papers.title: Positive Geometry of Oriented Matroid Strata
papers.abstract: We study the positive geometry of Grassmannians whose boundary is a union of Plücker divisors. For the full Plücker boundary the regions are closures of realization spaces of uniform oriented matroids. In rank three we show that the pair $(\mathrm{Gr}_{3,n},Z_{3,n})$ is a positive arrangement in the sense of Sturmfels and Telen for $n\le 9$ points and compute its combinatorial rank from point counts of the configuration space $\mathcal{X}_{3,n}$ over finite fields. For seven points the canonical forms of the regions span all logarithmic forms. For eight points they do not, because the Möbius-Kantor configuration is not realizable over the reals. This determines for seven and eight points whether the integrands of Cachazo, Early and Zhang for the generalized biadjoint amplitudes of Cachazo, Early, Guevara and Mizera span the space of logarithmic forms. From ten points on, the genus is positive because a K3 surface appears in the boundary. For smaller boundaries and arbitrary rank we give a recursion that adds one point at a time and preserves the genus and the combinatorial rank. It recovers the positive Grassmannian and shows that realization spaces of stacked polytopes are regions of positive arrangements of combinatorial rank one.

papers.title: The Universal Frame Characterization of C*-algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that a C*-algebra A is a C*-algebra of compact operators if and only if every Hilbert A-module admits a frame. This answers affirmatively the question of Amini, Asadi, Elliott and Khosravi (2017), arising from the problem of Frank and Larson (2002)

papers.title: From hockey stick to boomerang via Appell polynomials
papers.abstract: In Pascal's triangle, the hockey-stick identities are well known as certain sums over the binomial coefficients, e.g., lying in a fixed row or column of the triangle. We establish unified identities that are connected with Appell polynomials, from which the hockey-stick identities follow as a very special case. Subsequently, we derive several identities for (reciprocal) Appell polynomials yielding applications to the Bernoulli and Euler polynomials. As a result, we obtain new identities for the Bernoulli, Euler, Fibonacci, and Genocchi numbers, as well as, power sums. This also leads to infinitely many recurrence relations for these numbers.

papers.title: Analytic properties of Boolean-Narayana numbers
papers.abstract: Very recently, Bóna introduced the Boolean-Narayana numbers BoNa(n,k) as the number of 0-1-trees on n+1 vertices with k right edges. We prove the total positivity of the Boolean-Narayana triangle by providing an explicit matrix factorization, and construct a planar digraph for this triangle. We give two combinatorial interpretations of the gamma-coefficients of the Boolean-Narayana polynomials. We also show the strong q-log-convexity of the Boolean-Narayana polynomials and the asymptotic normality of the Boolean-Narayana numbers. A bijection between 0-1-trees and colored Motzkin paths is constructed, presenting an alternative interpretation of the Boolean-Narayana numbers.

papers.title: Sharp Casorati Inequalities for Pointwise Bi-Slant Riemannian Maps into Sasakian Space Forms
papers.abstract: We establish Casorati inequalities for pointwise bi-slant Riemannian maps into Sasakian space forms with the characteristic vector field tangent to the range. The Sasakian structure imposes specific conditions on the second fundamental form, leading to refined inequalities for the normalized horizontal scalar curvature that also account for O'Neill's tensor. For proper pointwise bi-slant maps, equality in the two principal inequalities is characterized by the vanishing of the second fundamental form on the orthogonal complement of the characteristic direction in the range. We also derive corresponding inequalities for pointwise semi-slant, hemi-slant, and slant Riemannian maps and construct examples attaining equality.

papers.title: On Waring's problem for fourth powers
papers.abstract: We prove that every sufficiently large integer $n$, satisfying $n\equiv 1,2,3,\dots,11\pmod*{16}$, can be written as a sum of $11$ biquadrates. In particular, $G^{\#}(4)\leq 11$. This improves upon $G^{\#}(4)\leq 12$ due to Vaughan in 1989.

papers.title: An intrinsic criterion for Pansu differentials to be homomorphisms of nilpotent Lie groups
papers.abstract: By Pansu's theorem, Lipschitz maps between Carnot groups are differentiable almost everywhere, and their differentials are group homomorphisms. When the domain is instead a nilpotent Lie group with a bracket-generating left-invariant distribution, the Pansu differential is a homomorphism of an osculating Carnot group, which depends on an auxiliary choice of grading, and it need not be a homomorphism of the original group. We give an intrinsic criterion for when it is one, for a suitable choice of grading: the differential must vanish on an ideal that depends only on the group and its distribution, and comes from a universal quotient onto a Carnot group. The criterion holds automatically when the step of the target is small enough, and an explicit example shows that this threshold is sharp. Along the way, we determine exactly how the obstruction depends on the choice of grading.

papers.title: Ancient solutions of mean curvature flow in a slab
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study complete ancient solutions of the mean curvature flow in arbitrary codimension contained in slabs in Euclidean space. Under a natural principal-angle condition, we prove that a translating soliton contained in a slab of width less than $π$ cannot be bounded from below in the translating direction, and characterize the grim reaper cylinder in form of a rigidity result at the critical width $π$. We derive corresponding results for ancient solutions confined in slabs.

papers.title: Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems
papers.abstract: Zariski-van Kampen theorems are meant to constitute a complement to Lefschetz-Zariski theorems which, in turn, generalize the classical Lefschetz theorem on hyperplane sections to quasi-projective varieties or to the corresponding local case. Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems are developed here as a tool which is useful both in the local and in the global case.

papers.title: Convexification effects of $L_p$-sums
papers.abstract: It is a classical result, quantified by Shapley, Folkman, and Starr, that the Minkowski averages of any compact set asymptotically approach its convex hull in the Hausdorff metric. In this paper, we investigate the analogous convexification phenomenon for the Firey $L_p$-sums of compact sets. First, we establish new structural properties of the $L_p$-sum. Notably, we show that the iterated $L_p$-sum of compact sets whose convex hull contains the origin is eventually starlike. We then study $L_p$-convexification for three classical measures of nonconvexity: Hausdorff metric, volume deficit, and effective standard deviation. For each of these measures, we prove that the $k$-fold $L_p$-sum averages of a compact set $A$ converge to $\text{conv}(0,A)$ when $1<p<\infty$, and to $\text{conv}(A)$ when $p=\infty$. In each case, we show that the convergence to the convex hull is eventually monotone. For the Hausdorff metric and effective standard deviation, we prove sharp upper bounds for the $L_p$-sum of two compact sets.

papers.title: Counting periodic points of rational self-maps of projective varieties
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the number of isolated periodic points of a dominant rational self-map of a smooth projective variety. We first give an upper bound for this number in terms of the degrees of the iterates of the map, thereby extending a theorem of Dinh--Nguyen--Truong to arbitrary characteristic. Our approach is purely algebraic and bypasses the theory of densities of positive closed currents. We then establish the exact asymptotic growth of isolated periodic points of birational self-maps of surfaces over a field of characteristic 0. To do so, we extend Jonsson--Reschke's argument to any finitely generated field over $ \mathbb Q $ using Moriwaki's theory of heights.

papers.title: A short proof of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture
papers.abstract: We give a short alternative proof of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture, recently proved by OpenAI. Our proof combines their reduction with a different argument showing that every nontrivial oriented graph $G$ contains a nonempty set $X$ such that $X^+\ne V(G)$ and $|(X^+)^+\setminus X^+|\geq|X^+\setminus X|$, where $X^+=N_G^+[X]$.

papers.title: Gorenstein symmetry can fail for noetherian rings
papers.abstract: We construct a two-sided noetherian ring $A$ which has injective dimension $1$ as a left module over itself and infinite injective dimension as a right module over itself. This shows that Gorenstein symmetry can fail for two-sided noetherian rings. It is further shown that there is such an example over any field of characteristic different than $2$, that it has a dualizing complex, and that its derived category of right modules does not satisfy injective-generation in the sense of Rickard-Keller.

papers.title: On the Fujii conjectures
papers.abstract: Using the Riemann hypothesis for the nonprincipal character modulo four, we disprove Fujii's first conjecture on exponential weights and prove his second conjecture on iterated weights by Mellin convolution [Proc. Japan Acad. Ser. A Math. Sci. 64 (1988), 260--263]. Further, we unify the two conjectures through a two-parameter family of Mellin kernels and prove that the prime race exhibits a phase transition.

papers.title: ab-indices for lattice path matroids
papers.abstract: The base polytopes of connected lattice path matroids admit subdivisions into snakes. We use these to obtain an explicit positive combinatorial description of their ab-indices, their Chow polynomials and their chain polynomials. We finally apply this description to the particular case of the ab-index of Schubert matroids.

papers.title: Patterson-Sullivan Theory for Approximate Groups
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the limit set of a uniformly discrete approximate subgroup acting on a negatively curved manifold, and prove several properties comparable to that of the classical case of discrete groups, including a version of the dichotomy between elementary and non-elementary groups. Furthermore, we adapt the Patterson-Sullivan construction for discrete groups to obtain asymptotic counting results for the orbits of infinite uniformly discrete approximate groups acting on a negatively curved manifold.

papers.title: An approach to topology via lattices of names
papers.abstract: Synthetic topology encompasses various alternatives to the classical definition of a topological space by Hausdorff. In particular, Abstract Stone Duality (ASD) develops the theory of locally compact spaces directly from logic. This study introduces a semi-formal theory of synthetic topology using a first-order version of the intuitionistic modal logic iS4, inspired by a nominalist, dynamic interpretation of the specialization order. The remarkable similarities to ASD include a constructive interpretation of the open-closed duality, overtness of the line, compactness of the unit interval and the nuclei that define closed and open subspaces.

papers.title: Even Quartets and the Maximum Density of a Simplical 3-Cocycle
papers.abstract: Colour the triples of an $n$-element set red or blue, and call a four-set even if it contains an even number of red triples. We prove that the minimum number of even four-sets is $\frac5{16}\binom n4-Θ(n^3)$. In particular, the maximum asymptotic density of a simplicial $3$-cocycle over the field of two elements is $11/16$. The classical two-part matrix construction attains the limiting bound. We prove that it also determines the unique limiting distribution of quartet parities on every fixed number of vertices. Writing $m_n$ for the minimum density, we bound the limit inferior and limit superior of $n(5/16-m_n)$ between $0.75$ and $0.752427$. The lower bound on even quartets follows from an exact rational inequality on eight vertices. A perturbation of the construction explains all $72$ cases of equality in this finite inequality, of which only $22$ survive in an extremal limit.

papers.title: Sharp variational estimates for Schrödinger equation in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: We study strong $r$-variation estimates for the free Schrödinger equation on $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq3$. Combining fractal and weighted restriction estimates with mixed space--time estimates, we determine the sharp Sobolev regularity, up to endpoints, in several ranges of the spatial exponent $p$ and the variation exponent $r$. In particular, our results give a sharp $L^2(\mathbb R^n)$ variational extension of the Schrödinger maximal estimate of Du and Zhang [\emph{Ann. of Math.}, \textbf{189}, 837--861 (2019)].

papers.title: Default-Distance Entropy and Metric Dimension in Finite Geometries
papers.abstract: A resolving set in a graph is a set of landmarks whose distance vectors distinguish all vertices. We use information theory to prove lower bounds for metric dimension and class dimension in distance-regular graphs and association schemes arising from finite geometry. The core idea is that, for a fixed landmark, a random object usually lies in one overwhelmingly likely distance or relation class. For classical dual polar graphs, with rank and type fixed and $q\to\infty$ through the admissible field orders, we prove $μ(Γ(q,d,e))=Θ_{d,e}(q^e)$ for $d\geq 2$ and $e>0$. The lower bound uses opposition as the typical distance. For the upper bound, we take, for each of a constant number of $(d-1)$-dimensional singular subspaces, all generators containing it. For Grassmann graphs, bilinear forms graphs, and attenuated-space schemes, we obtain lower bounds of the same exponential order as the known incidence constructions.

papers.title: Higher Order Structure along Nilpotent Eigendirections in Planar Vector Fields
papers.abstract: We study a distinguished one dimensional restriction associated with planar vector fields whose linearization is a nonzero nilpotent matrix of index two. This restriction admits an intrinsic interpretation on the nilpotent eigendirection, while its scalar representation in Jordan coordinates satisfies a simple transformation law under admissible changes of Jordan chain. Its quadratic Taylor coefficient coincides with the intrinsic quadratic Bogdanov--Takens coefficient. % For rational restrictions, we show that the Taylor coefficient sequence satisfies a finite linear recurrence determined by the minimal denominator. Its degree defines a recurrence degree that is invariant under admissible changes of Jordan chain and gives the minimal order of an eventual homogeneous recurrence. Exact cancellations may therefore be detected directly from the restriction before nonlinear normal form transformations are performed. Applications to four planar models exhibit different recurrence degree and cancellation mechanisms, illustrating the complementarity between the distinguished restriction and smooth nilpotent normal form theory.

papers.title: A normal form for the Thin Flat Surfaces category
papers.abstract: The category TFS of thin flat surfaces, introduced by Khovanov, Qi, and Rozansky, is a strict symmetric monoidal category whose morphisms are compact oriented surfaces with corners arising as neighbourhoods of immersed graphs in a strip. We prove two main results. First, a normal form theorem: every connected viewable tf-cobordism is equal, in TFS, to a canonical composite determined by its topological type. Second, a sufficiency theorem: we establish a list of relations in the TFS category which are sufficient, meaning that any two composites of generators representing the same tf-cobordism are related by a finite sequence of the listed relations. Together, these results give a complete generators-and-relations presentation of TFS.

papers.title: The Segre invariant and Brill-Noether theory on Hirzebruch surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the Segre invariant on rank two $H$-stable vector bundles with fixed Chern classes on Hirzebruch surfaces $Σ_{n}$. For each vector bundle on these surfaces, we determine the possible values of the Segre invariant and compute the number of global sections of these bundles and present applications to Brill-Noether Theory.

papers.title: $K_2$-regularity is equivalent to smoothness for toric varieties
papers.abstract: Recent work by Wanchun Shen shows that $K_2$-regular affine local complete intersections of any dimension in characteristic zero are smooth. In this note, we show that the same holds for affine toric varieties.

papers.title: Countable Graphs with Finite Path-width: Characterisation and Universality
papers.abstract: We study path-width and the closely related parameter line-width in countably infinite graphs. Our first result characterises the graphs of finite path-width: they are the graphs that do not have infinitely many vertices of infinite degree, do not have infinitely many pairwise disjoint infinite paths, and contain no subdivision of some finite tree of maximum degree 3. We then investigate universality under the subgraph relation for graphs of bounded path-width or line-width. In particular, we prove that there exists a universal graph with line-width $\mathcal{O}(k^2)$ for the class of graphs with line-width at most $k$. In contrast, we show that no graph of finite path-width is universal for the class of locally finite graphs with path-width $1$. Finally, we show that for each $k\geq 2$, every universal graph for the class of graphs with path-width at most $k$ has line-width at least $k + 1$.

papers.title: The role of parameter Jacobians in the stability of network outputs
papers.abstract: In the framework of network dynamics, learning models, and neural tangent kernels (NTK), we show that the corresponding linearized dynamics leads naturally to a semigroup formulation. More precisely, in our analysis of input/output models, the time-dynamics is presented via special semigroups of linear operators on Hilbert spaces, together with an associated class of semigroup perturbations. In this context, we then present new and explicit a priori perturbation-bound results: for the fixed-kernel linearization constructions arising in the NTK setting, we prove norm-bounds on the corresponding semigroup perturbations, in the form of explicit finite-time perturbation estimates. We further present refinements on prescribed task spaces, Cesàro-averaged (ergodic) comparisons estimates, and versions in which the lower spectral edge assumption is replaced by a spectral-distribution condition. We also extend the comparison to nonautonomous NTK evolutions through piecewise-frozen approximations, record a corresponding discrete Euler specialization, and offer worked examples in order to illustrate our perturbation-bound estimates.

papers.title: An Erdős-Wintner theorem for second-order linear recurrent bases
papers.abstract: Let $a,b$ be integers with $1\le b\le a$, and let \[ G_0=1,\qquad G_1=a+1,\qquad G_{n+2}=aG_{n+1}+bG_n. \] For real-valued functions which are additive in the greedy $G$-digits, we prove a necessary-and-sufficient criterion for the existence of a limiting distribution. The criterion consists of a first-order drift series and a quadratic digit-energy series, and it recovers the Zeckendorf theorem when $a=b=1$. The main difficulty is necessity: a one-step transfer matrix detects all non-maximal digit values, while the maximal digit becomes visible only in a two-step product. A weighted Euclidean norm symmetrizes the untwisted companion matrix and makes both contractions occur at the true Perron scale. Sufficiency follows from a two-dimensional Perron product lemma with square-summable transverse perturbations and a convergent, not necessarily absolutely convergent, Perron drift. The limiting characteristic function admits a scalar infinite-product representation in a neighbourhood of the origin and a global matrix-product representation at arbitrary frequencies.

papers.title: Singularity Categories of Simple Singularities in Positive Characteristic
papers.abstract: We study the singularity categories of simple singularities of the same dimension over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, and show that, as in characteristic zero, these categories are not equivalent as triangulated categories unless the underlying singularities are analytically isomorphic. In contrast to the characteristic zero case, simple singularities in positive characteristic cannot be distinguished solely from the Auslander-Reiten quivers of their singularity categories. To address this, we extend to positive characteristics a theorem by Hua and Keller, which asserts that the 0th Hochschild cohomology of the dg singularity category of an isolated hypersurface singularity in characteristic zero is isomorphic to the Tyurina algebra of the defining polynomial. Furthermore as an application, we determine the condition for the singularity category of a rational double point (i.e., a simple singularity of dimension two) to be standard. We prove that such a category is standard if and only if the defining polynomial is weighted homogeneous.

papers.title: Trilinear Kloosterman fractions II: subdyadic intervals and nearly balanced convolutions
papers.abstract: This paper broadens the range on which Fouvry and Radziwiłł's results on nearly balanced convolutions apply. In particular, let $α_m$ and $β_n$ be sequences supported on $m\sim M$ and $n\sim N$ where $β_n$ is equidistributed for small moduli, and let $Q=X^{\frac 12+\varepsilon}$. We find that \begin{gather*}\sum_{q\sim Q}\left|\mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{n\sim N,m\sim M \\ mn\equiv a\pmod q}}α_mβ_n-\frac{1}{φ(q)}\mathop{\sum\sum}_{\substack{n\sim N,m\sim M \\ (mn,q)=1}}α_mβ_n\right|\ll \frac{X}{\log^A X} \end{gather*} if $N=X^{\frac 12+δ}$ and $M=X^{\frac 12-δ}$ with $0<δ<\frac 1{68}$, which improves Fouvry and Radziwiłł's $0<δ<\frac 1{112}$. To prove this, we sharpen Bettin and Chandee's famous result on trilinear forms with Kloosterman fractions in the case where some of the sums are over subdyadic intervals.

papers.title: Zero-free columns in character tables of symmetric groups
papers.abstract: The rows and columns of the character table of the symmetric group $S_n$ are both naturally indexed by partitions of $n$. Let $D(n)$ denote the number of conjugacy classes of $S_n$ whose column contains no zero entry. The identity column is always zero-free, so $D(n)\geq 1$. It is known that $D(n)\ll n^2$. We prove that $D(n)\ll n^{3/4}$. Second, we prove for almost all positive integers $n$ that $D(n)\ll_B n^{1/2}(\log n)^B$ for every $B>5/6$, with a quantitative bound for the exceptional set, using work of Matomäki and Radziwill. Finally, we offer a heuristic supporting our conjecture that $D(n)\ll_{\varepsilon} n^{\varepsilon}$. AxiomProver formalized the results in this paper in Lean assuming preexisting literature.

papers.title: On Lipschitz Spaces, Semigroup Transference, and Heat Kernel Derivative Estimates in Dunkl--Schrödinger Analysis
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Lipschitz spaces adapted to Dunkl--Schrödinger operators $\mathcal{L} = -Δ_k + V$, where $Δ_k$ is the Dunkl Laplacian and $V \ge 0$ belongs to the reverse Hölder class $\mathrm{RH}^q(dw)$ with $q > \max(1, \mathbf{N}/2)$. For $0 < β< 2$, we establish the full equivalence between the heat semigroup-based Lipschitz spaces $\widetildeΛ_{\mathcal{L},k}^{β/2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$ and the pointwise weighted Zygmund classes $Λ_{\mathcal{L},k}^β(\mathbb{R}^N)$ defined via the critical radius function $m(\mathbf{x})$. Remarkably, this characterization shows that the spatial smoothness component decouples completely from the underlying reflection group symmetries and root systems. As an intermediate result, we establish new equivalences for inhomogeneous weighted Lipschitz spaces associated with the unperturbed Dunkl Laplacian $Δ_k$. A central difficulty in this context --- arising from the necessity to disentangle the Euclidean distance from the orbit metric $d(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ --- is resolved through a detailed geometric analysis. Finally, we provide pointwise Gaussian upper bounds for the time derivatives of the Dunkl--Schrödinger heat kernel, which are of independent interest for future work in harmonic analysis on Dunkl structures. Crucially, we do not assume the potential $V$ to be $G$-invariant under the action of the Weyl group, which introduces major geometric difficulties resolved here via a local analysis of the orbit metric.

papers.title: The Eigenvalue Region of a Family of Markov Chains with Randomness Confined to Two States
papers.abstract: We determine the complete eigenvalue region of the following Markov chains on $2q$ states, for $q\ge2$. The states are $A_0,\ldots,A_{q-1}$ and $B_0,\ldots,B_{q-1}$. Each transition $A_j\to A_{j+1}$ and $B_j\to B_{j+1}$, for $0\le j<q-1$, has probability one. From $A_{q-1}$, the chain moves to $A_0$ with probability $a$ and to $B_0$ with probability $1-a$. From $B_{q-1}$, it moves to $B_0$ with probability $b$ and to $A_j$ with probability $(1-b)p_j$. Here $a,b\in[0,1]$ and $p_j\ge0$ with $\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}p_j=1$; these parameters vary over all permitted values. Every segment from zero to an attainable eigenvalue lies in the region. Its unit-circle points are exactly the roots of unity of order at most $2q$, as for unrestricted stochastic matrices of the same order, yet the full region is strictly smaller. It excludes $0<|\operatorname{Arg}λ|<π/q$. For odd $q$, the final nonreal boundary arc ends at a negative real point inside the unit disk; the remaining interval to $-1$ is also boundary. Every transition matrix has the same characteristic polynomial as one with $a=b$. Among $q+1$ fixed matrices in this balanced family, convex combinations of at most three realize every attainable eigenvalue, and two suffice on the boundary. Both bounds are sharp within this set. Consecutive reduced fractions in $[1/(2q),1/2]$ with denominators at most $2q$ select the upper nonreal boundary constructions. Each boundary radius is the unique solution of an equation whose left-hand side increases strictly with the radius.

papers.title: Spacetime closedness theorem for homogeneous Lorentzian foliations
papers.abstract: Motivated by the geometric interpretation of spatially homogeneous cosmological models, we formulate a spacetime closedness theorem directly at the Lorentzian level. A classical space-form classification theorem organizes homogeneous and isotropic spatial geometries, but by itself it does not yield a Lorentzian statement about the ambient spacetime. The main technical step is to derive finite slice-volume from genuinely Lorentzian control hypotheses on the foliation. This is achieved in a strong version, for maximally regular globally hyperbolic $(n+1)$--spacetimes with a finite-time Big Bang and homogeneous complete spacelike slices, and in a weaker version in which maximal regularity is replaced by time-integrability of the accumulated expansion rate. In both cases, the argument separates an analytic step, deriving finite slice-volume from the Big Bang and temporal control, from a geometric step, upgrading finite volume to compactness by homogeneity and completeness. The theorem is stated in arbitrary spacetime dimension and is accompanied by a Lean~4 formalization of the strong and weak abstract statements.

papers.title: Diophantine m-tuples of Triangular Numbers
papers.abstract: A $m$-tuple with the property $D(n)$ is a tuple of $m$ positive integers $(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_m)$ such that $a_i a_j + n$ is an square, for $1 \le i < j \le m$. The $k$th triangular number is $T_k = \frac{k(k+1)}{2}$ for nonnegative integers $k$. We consider $D(1)$ tuples consisting only of triangular numbers. We prove the nonexistence of any $D(1)$ triangular quadruple and describe an algorithm to generate an infinite family of $D(1)$ triangular triples, which we conjecture contains all $D(1)$ triangular triples. We also consider general $D(n)$ tuples. To aid with computational difficulties, we present an efficient algorithm, using Generalized Pell Equations (GPEs), to determine whether $T_a$ is in a $D(n)$ triangular pair, which runs in $O(a^{1/2})$ time. We then prove that no $D(n)$ triangular pair exists for $n \equiv 2,5 \text{ (mod } 9\text{)}$, and discuss other values of $n$ for which there appear to be no $D(n)$ triangular pairs. We also show that our $D(n)$ equation has solutions in all $\mathbb{Q}_p$, for $p \neq 3$. We then present progress on determining a general criteria on $n$ for which no $D(n)$ triangular pairs exist.

papers.title: Finding large families of rational curves through Bend-and-Break
papers.abstract: We present a new construction that allows us to break off large-degree rational curves from families of higher genus curves. Our construction and results deepen the connection between rational curves and positivity of the anticanonical divisor. Specifically, we show that varieties with large Fujita invariant admit large families of rational curves. We also construct free rational curves on certain singular Fano varieties. As an explicit consequence of our results, we prove that for a general Fano hypersurface of index at least 3, all spaces of genus g curves of sufficiently large degree have the expected dimension.

papers.title: Majority C-coloring in Cartesian products
papers.abstract: A majority C-coloring of a graph $G$ assigns colors to the vertices such that every vertex shares its color with at least half of its neighbors. The maximum number of colors that can be used in such a coloring of $G$ is denoted by $\overlineχ_{\geqslant}(G)$. In this paper, the focus is on the majority C-coloring in Cartesian product graphs. It is shown that $\overlineχ_{\geqslant}(G \square H) \ge \overlineχ_{\geqslant}(G) \overlineχ_{\geqslant}(H)$ gives a sharp lower bound, but the difference also can be arbitrarily large. For two-dimensional Hamming graphs, the exact value $\overlineχ_{\geqslant}(K_m \square K_n) = \min\{m,n\}$ is established. Balanced Hamming graphs of higher dimension, that is the $k$th powers of complete graphs with respect to the Cartesian product, are also studied. It is proved that $\overlineχ_{\geqslant}(K_n^{\square, k})= n^{k/2}$ holds for every even integer $k$. If $k$ is odd and the Hamming graph is the $k$-dimensional hypercube, then $\overlineχ_{\geqslant}(K_2^{\square, k})= 2^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}$. On the other hand, a majority C-coloring of $K_n^{\square, k}$ with at least $3 n^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}/2 $ colors is presented for every $n \ge 7$ and odd $k \ge 3$. For Cartesian grids, the main result shows that $\overlineχ_{\geqslant}(P_m \square P_n) = 1 + \lfloor m/2\rfloor \lfloor n/2\rfloor$ if at least one of $m$ and $n$ is odd, while $\overlineχ_{\geqslant}(P_m \square P_n)=mn/4$ holds if both parameters are even and $m \ge n \ge 4$. The paper concludes with a conjecture and several open problems.

papers.title: A categorical model structure for generalized algebraic theories
papers.abstract: We describe a (combinatorial, monoidal, Cat-enriched) Quillen model structure on the category of Cartmell's generalized algebraic theories (gats); its homotopy bicategory consists essentially of Taylor's rooted display map categories. This allows us to compare two kinds of morphisms of gats: one where sort dependency and substitution are preserved strictly, thus directly matching the syntax, and one where the given structure is preserved up to isomorphism. We prove a strictification result for morphisms out of cofibrant theories, which are the retracts of theories without sort equality axioms. Along the way, we give a structural characterization of when a contextual category can be presented without sort equality axioms. Our results also imply that when restricted to cofibrant objects, the tensor product of gats has the expected semantic behaviour, namely, it corresponds to the tensor product of locally finitely presentable categories equipped with a cofibrantly generated weak factorization system. Strict and weak morphisms specialize, respectively, to two familiar concepts of model of a gat A: ones valued in iterated families of sets, with substitution interpreted as reindexing, and set-valued models of the contextual category C(A) viewed as a finite-limit sketch. We characterize strictifiability of a model of the latter kind via a loop freeness condition on a certain map of functors out of the category of context projections of A.

papers.title: Cartan Determinants in algebraic geometry
papers.abstract: We formulate a dg-categorical analogue of the Cartan determinant conjecture using numerical Grothendieck groups. Let $D$ be a smooth proper dg category over an algebraically closed field $k$. The Euler pairing on $K_0(D)$ descends to a nondegenerate bilinear form on the numerical Grothendieck group $K_{\mathrm{num}}(D)$, and hence defines a numerical Cartan determinant $\det M_χ(D)$. While the classical Cartan determinant conjecture predicts that $\det M_χ(A)=1$ for finite-dimensional smooth algebras $A$, this equality is no longer expected for general smooth proper dg categories. However, we propose the following positivity question: $\det M_χ(D)>0.$ Our main result proves this positivity when $D=\operatorname{Perf}(X)$ for a large class of smooth projective varieties $X$. More precisely, we show that $\det M_χ(X)>0$ if either $\dim X$ is odd, or $X$ has even dimension and satisfies the numerical Hodge standard conjecture.

papers.title: Acyclic and totally acyclic objects in the $Q$-shaped derived category
papers.abstract: This paper concerns homological algebra based on $Q$-shaped diagrams, where $Q$ belongs to a certain class of small categories. We will show that the Gorenstein property of noetherian commutative rings is characterised by the condition that acyclicity coincides with total acyclicity for $Q$-shaped diagrams of suitable classes of modules. Many special cases occur as corollaries, for instance $N$-complexes. This generalises a classic result by Iyengar and Krause to the programme of $Q$-shaped derived categories, which builds on an insight of Iyama and Minamoto. We prove our result using an adjoint triple of functors relating $Q$-shaped diagrams to chain complexes. One of the functors was introduced by Jasso, and the whole triple generalises the compression, cocompression, and expansion functors for differential modules introduced by Avramov, Buchweitz, and Iyengar and by Nkansah. We consider the adjoint triple to be the main contribution of this paper.

papers.title: Stein Kernels and Normal Approximation for Log-Concave Bilinear Forms
papers.abstract: Jiang, Lee, and Vempala conjectured that if $X,Y\in\mathbb{R}^n$ are independent isotropic log-concave random vectors, then $W_2(L(\langle X,Y\rangle),N(0,n))$ is bounded by a universal constant. Subject to Theorems 1.2 and 2.5 of arXiv:2607.24164v1, we prove this conjecture and a rectangular bilinear-form extension. For independent isotropic log-concave $X\in\mathbb{R}^m$, $Y\in\mathbb{R}^n$, and nonzero $B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, put \[ r_4(B)=\frac{(\operatorname{Tr}(B^\top B))^2} {\operatorname{Tr}((B^\top B)^2)}. \] We construct a nonnegative scalar Stein kernel for $X^\top B Y/\|B\|_F$ whose squared $L^2$ discrepancy is at most $20/r_4(B)$, and consequently obtain the same bound for squared $2$-Wasserstein distance to $N(0,1)$. The proof develops an exact covariance identity and deficit decomposition for trace observables of moment-map Stein kernels, together with a stability theorem for positive Stein kernels under log-concave approximation. Taking $B=I_n$ yields \[ W_2^2\left(L\left(\frac{\langle X,Y\rangle}{\sqrt{n}}\right),N(0,1)\right)\leq\frac{20}{n}, \] which is the Jiang--Lee--Vempala conjecture.

papers.title: Orbifold Degenerations of Hirzebruch Surfaces
papers.abstract: We study orbifold degenerations of Hirzebruch surfaces. Our main theorem shows that every such degeneration $X$ arises as a partial smoothing of a toric surface. We then give a combinatorial description of the singularities that arise when $-K_X$ is not nef. This complements previous joint work with G. Urzúa, which treated the case in which $-K_X$ is ample. For Hirzebruch surfaces $\mathbb{F}_k$ with $k\geq 3$, we obtain an explicit description of all possible central fibers. For $k\leq 1$, we use the threefold minimal model program to reduce the problem to the case of central fibers whose anticanonical divisor is nef. The remaining surfaces are toric del Pezzo surfaces of degree $8$ with T-singularities. We classify these by studying the birational geometry arising from mutations of Fano polygons.

papers.title: Algebraic implicitization techniques in the graphical models program
papers.abstract: Many aspects of daily life now rely on technology driven by advanced techniques for analyzing multivariate data. Graphical models provide the general framework within which much of these analyses take place. However, different data types require different graphical models, with each requiring its own basic mathematical theory to guide sound statistical inference. Developing this theory for a family of graphical models requires solutions to fundamental questions, where emerging mathematical approaches are utilizing what can collectively be called algebraic implicitization techniques. These notes provide an introduction to the basics of graphical models and the algebraic implicitization techniques now appearing in instances of the graphical models program.

papers.title: Uniformly Weighted Graphical Designs
papers.abstract: A graphical design is a subset of vertices of a graph, along with a weight for each chosen vertex, that can perfectly average chosen subspaces of functions on the graph. A design is uniformly weighted if all the weights are equal, and several well-known combinatorial objects such as orthogonal arrays, combinatorial block designs and t-wise permutations are uniformly weighted graphical designs. While one might expect to see uniformly weighted designs in structured graphs, they do not always exist. In this paper we characterize the existence of uniformly weighted graphical designs, and use our result to provide several families of graphs that have, and do not have, such designs. Our results offer a polyhedral view of the structures that control the existence and cardinalities of these designs. In particular, we characterize all uniformly weighted designs of threshold graphs, and provide a geometric proof of the duality of linear codes and linear orthogonal arrays. We also provide a novel construction for graphs whose Laplacian characteristic polynomials are almost irreducible, to produce families without uniformly weighted designs.

papers.title: A functional model for hyponormal contractions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical model for a class of hyponormal contractions $T$ satisfying $Ran[T^*,T] \subseteq \mathcal D_{T^*}\ominus \mathcal D_T$, where $\mathcal D_{T^*}$ and $\mathcal D_T$ are the associated defect spaces for $T$. We also show that, under a certain condition, a contraction $T$ with $\mathcal D_T \subseteq \mathcal D_{T^*}$ is hyponormal.

papers.title: Optimal polynomial meshes beyond geometric boundary regularity via Green sublevels
papers.abstract: We establish a potential-theoretic sufficient condition for a compact subset of the real line to admit an optimal polynomial mesh. The criterion bounds the cardinality of a norming set by a linear term in the polynomial degree plus the number of connected components of a Green sublevel at height $α/n$, where $α>0$ is fixed. By combining this principle with an estimate due to Andrievskii, we prove that every uniformly perfect compact subset of $\mathbb{R}$ admits an optimal polynomial mesh. A standard product argument then produces optimal meshes on finite Cartesian products; in particular, it yields an optimal mesh on the planar Cantor dust $C\times C$, which is self-similar, totally disconnected, and has empty interior.

papers.title: On symmetricity of orthogonality with respect to numerical radius norm
papers.abstract: We study Birkhoff-James orthogonality and local symmetric points in the space $C(K,X)$ of vector-valued continuous functions equipped with a numerical-radius type (semi-)norm. We extend the theory of abstract numerical ranges to semi-normed spaces and obtain complete characterizations of the left and right symmetric points of $C(K,X)$ with respect to the numerical-radius (semi-) norm. We also establish corresponding results for the space $\mathcal{K}(X)$ of compact operators on $X$.

papers.title: Sharp Order Laws and Finite-Defect Stability for Domination versus Small Laplacian Eigenvalues in Trees
papers.abstract: For a tree T, let gamma(T) be its domination number and let mu(T) count the Laplacian eigenvalues in [0,1). The strict inequality gamma(T)/mu(T)<4/3 leaves open three linked questions: the exact finite-order defect, the structure near equality, and whether a fixed defect permits only finitely many local obstructions. We answer all three. For every n>=2, max_{|V(T)|=n} (7 gamma(T)-9 mu(T)) = floor((n-20)/9). Thus order twenty-nine is the first at which the ratio 9/7 can be exceeded. The proof is based on an exact decomposition of Phi(T)=|V(T)|-20-9(7 gamma(T)-9 mu(T)) into nonnegative integer terms, together with a clean-contraction identity. For subcubic trees, equality cases are canonical lifts of trees with perfect matchings. We classify every layer through Phi=42, locating successive phase transitions at 20, 21, 40, 41, and 42. The finiteness mechanism is simple to state: after the repeatable matched-skeleton pieces are removed, fixed slack leaves only a bounded exceptional core. Formally, a local compactness theorem bounds every nonordinary weighted deep component at fixed packing surplus and residual negative index. Consequently, for each fixed k, every subcubic tree with Phi(T)=k consists of a bounded ported defect kernel, an arbitrary compatible forest of ordinary tiles, and at most floor(k/21) clean expansions. All unbounded statements are proved symbolically; exact computation is used only for explicitly bounded atom lists and independent finite verification.

papers.title: Who Pays for a Connected Public Good?
papers.abstract: Connectivity can turn separate contributions into a public good that benefits participants and nonparticipants alike. Yet only participants pay for it, and each can avoid her charge by withdrawing while enjoying whatever public output survives. How do network connections constrain who can or must pay, and how large a cost can the group bear? We study a participation game in which public output equals the size of the largest connected group of active players, whose members divide a fixed operating cost. The output a participant destroys by withdrawing is her withdrawal responsibility and bounds her payment. These bounds determine the group's cost-bearing capacity and, whenever the group can be kept active, which participants must pay. We prove that among connected networks with at least five players, the path uniquely maximizes the cost-bearing capacity of a group, yet minimizes the expected surviving output after a uniformly selected participant withdraws. As the group grows, the ratio of maximal capacity to gross social benefit under full participation converges to one quarter. Fragility can therefore strengthen voluntary finance, but even the most financeable network cannot close the gap between the value it creates and what its participants will pay to sustain it.

papers.title: Positive Geometry of Yang-Mills Correlators
papers.abstract: We develop a positive-geometric formulation of tree-level Yang-Mills correlators in de Sitter space at three and four points through their helicity-stripped representatives on the cosmological Grassmannian. In its Pfaffian (or spinor) embedding, physical singularities become natural geometric boundaries. At three points, the Yang-Mills correlator is the canonical form of the non-negative orthant in the Grassmannian. At four points, the Mandelstam divisors partition the Pfaffian-positive domain of the Grassmannian into four positive geometries. Requiring factorization into three-point forms, together with the correct flat-space limit, uniquely selects an oriented union of two of these regions, whose canonical form reproduces the reduced color-ordered Yang-Mills correlator. The full color-ordered correlator, on the other hand, arises from a uniquely fixed signed linear combination of homology cycles. Thus, the broader homological formulation of positive geometry is essential for capturing the complete four-point result. Our construction provides a concrete starting point for a geometric description of higher-point cosmological correlators.

papers.title: Cycle Counting and Character Expectations Using Alternating Structures
papers.abstract: Recently, three related papers [arXiv:2412.13941, arXiv:2009.00897, arXiv:2409.03626] found a connection between two subjects: the w-cycle theorem, which is a theorem about counting appearances of cycles reading out a word w in certain graphs, and character expectations on word measures. The w-cycle theorem was proven independently by [arXiv:1410.2540] using stackings and by [arXiv:1410.2579] using bislim structures. In the current work, we generalize stackings and bislim structures to alternating stackings and alternating bislim structures. We show how this significantly strengthens the w-cycle theorem for words admitting such alternating structures, and as a result, also strengthens the recent results of [arXiv:2412.13941] and [arXiv:2409.03626]. We show that generic words admit alternating bislim structures, and therefore, the strengthened results hold for generic words. Using our new machinery, we address conjectures of Wilton, of Hanany--Puder and of Puder--Shomroni. We prove that all three conjectures hold for generic words, but we also find counterexamples for the first two.

papers.title: Enumerating separable derangements
papers.abstract: We give a polynomial-time algorithm to compute the number $b_n$ of separable derangements of $[n]$. This algorithm is based on a generating function technique which tracks permutations along with their occupied diagonals, where each permutation is counted once for every such diagonal. We provide bounds for the proportion of separable permutations which are derangements, show that $b_n$ and the large Schröder numbers have the same exponential growth constant $(3 + 2 \sqrt{2})$, and use the first 3000 terms to conjecture more explicit asymptotic behavior. This partially answers several questions about separable derangements recently posed by Vatter.

papers.title: Groups satisfying Gaschütz's complement theorem
papers.abstract: A classical theorem of Gaschütz states that an abelian normal subgroup N of a finite group G has a complement in G whenever it has a complement in some subgroup H with $N \leq H \leq G$ and gcd(|N|, [G:H]) = 1. We characterize the finite groups N for which this theorem remains valid without the abelian hypothesis: this is the case if and only if $Z(N) \cap N' = 1$ and N has a complement in a quotient of the holomorph Hol(N) by a diagonal copy of N'. This completes a previous paper by the second author.

papers.title: Elementary divisors of the Cartan matrix for partial characters
papers.abstract: Let $π$ be a set of primes and let $G$ be a finite $π$-separable group. We prove that the Cartan matrix $C$ for the $π$-partial characters of $G$ is equivalent over the integers to a matrix $\operatorname{diag}(|\mathbf{C}_G(x)|_{π'})$, where $x$ runs over a set of representatives of the $π$-classes of $G$. In particular, we prove that $\det C = \prod |\mathbf{C}_G(x)|_{π'}.$

papers.title: Laplace and Dolbeault operators on Sasakian manifolds
papers.abstract: Sasakian manifolds, the odd-dimensional analogues of Kähler manifolds, carry two natural pairs of first-order Dolbeault-type operators on the full complex of differential forms, extending the Kohn--Rossi differentials. On such Sasaki manifolds, we establish Kähler-type identities for these operators, and relate the resulting Dolbeault Laplacians to the Hodge Laplacian. Unlike the Kähler case, where $Δ=2Δ_{\overline\partial}$, the relation has extra terms coming from the Reeb flow. Using these formulas and a Lefschetz decomposition, we derive lower and upper eigenvalue estimates for $Δ$ on forms depending on the eigenvalues of the Lie derivative of the Reeb vector field.

papers.title: Koszul duality and Morita categories
papers.abstract: We prove an $(\infty,2)$-categorical version of Koszul duality for operads and cooperads in spectra by showing that there is an equivalence between a Morita category of operads and bimodules and a dual Morita category of cooperads and bicomodules. This result subsumes various forms of operadic Koszul duality present in the literature.

papers.title: Towards the Global Torelli Theorem
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove finiteness results for K-trivial varieties in all dimensions. In dimension 2, these results are corollaries of the Global Torelli Theorem for polarized K3 surfaces. In particular, we establish a sufficient condition when two fibers of a projective family of K-trivial varieties are isomorphic via the Hodge theory. As applications, we prove that if a projective family of K-trivial varieties has a dense subset of birationally equivalent fibers, then all fibers are isomorphic.

papers.title: Graded Ehrhart theory for hypersimplices
papers.abstract: We prove that the $q$-Ehrhart series of a hyperplane slice of a cube is a rational function with an explicit denominator that satisfies $q$-reciprocity, confirming a conjecture of Reiner and Rhoades for these polytopes. To do this, we find a generating set for the orbit harmonics ideal, which also yields the Hilbert series and graded Frobenius characteristic of the associated quotient. We further show that the harmonic algebra of a hypersimplex $Δ$ is generated as an algebra by the harmonic space of $Δ$ using structural results on 2-factors of regular multigraphs. In particular, the harmonic algebra is finitely generated, giving a second proof of rationality.

papers.title: Disjoint and nearly disjoint sums of matrix multiplication tensors and their centroids
papers.abstract: This paper addresses centroids, which are fundamental invariants of tensors. Our main results are as follows: (i) The construction of explicit tensors with very large centroids, whereas previously it had been conjectured that none such exist. (ii) An upper bound on the dimension of the centroid that is essentially attained by our examples. (iii) The development of a geometric technique to write down border rank decomposition of tensors using centroids and "extended centroids". (iv) The technique is applied to tensors of this paper to prove they are of minimal border rank. The technique is versatile and enables us to geometrically derive and improve upon previous ad hoc decompositions. (v) The construction of symmetric tensors with large centroids and proof that they are wild in the sense of Buczyńska-Buczyński. Our results also pave the way for new upper bounds on the exponent of matrix multiplication.
